newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ukraine sees tax breaks to big foreign investors.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine sees tax breaks to big foreign investors.

text.p: Ukraine's government will consider extending tax breaks to foreign investors based on the size and strategic value of their investments, Serhiy Tyhypko, deputy prime minister in charge of reforms, said on Tuesday.
"We are ready to give individual consideration to those engaged in strategic investment," he told an investors conference.

Tyhypko said the government would lobby parliament "one more time" to re-instate a law, revoked from Tuesday, which had guaranteed tax and customs duties to companies which had begun working with a foreign investor before January 1, 1995.
But he said Ukraine could not easily afford tax breaks.

He did not say which companies could benefit from the strategic invesment policy but mentioned South Korea's Daewoo Group, which he said planned to invest $1.3 billion, as an example of the scale of investment.
He said Ukraine was not inclined to give tax breaks to small investors, particularly companies which might compete with Ukrainian firms in the flagging industrial sector.
The announcement of the tax break cancellation effective July 1 had provoked howls of protest from foreign investors in Ukraine.
Investors often criticise the former Soviet republic for an unwelcome investment climate consisting of conflicting laws, punitive taxes and corruption.
Foreigners have invested only $1.5 billion in Ukraine since its independence from the Soviet Union almost six years ago.
Daewoo will produce cars with U.S. company General Motors at the AvtoZAZ car plant in the city of Zaporizhya, and has also announced plans to build a hotel in the capital Kiev.
